sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 2002 (deposited 2014). Field notebook RB2-005, pp. 1-7 Kemak (speaker Rui Paulo de Jesus, b. 1966, Maliana, Bobonaro; sessions 18 Oct, 25 Oct, 1 Nov 2002). Kaipuleohone hdl:10125/33165, RB2-005-01.zip, images 001-008.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Unpublished wordlist notes, no statement about stress. Acute accents written on some forms, mostly penultimate ([siya] with accent on i, [ruwa], [telu], [lima], [pitu], [balu], [siwa], [sojo]; are, api, acu, mate, moas, modo, samalesu), but also final in timur 'Timorese', beya 'lie', agi 'wind' ('also heard as [agi] final-accented') and mane ~ mane 'man' (final when quick, penult when slow). Suggestive of penultimate stress with variation, but not a published statement.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 kema1243 reference list (15 refs). Note: Tomaschek et al. 2013, Ellis & Hardcastle 2002 and West 1999 are electromagnetic-articulography ('EMA') phonetics papers mis-attached to Ema/Kemak; Schaefer 1987 is Emai (Nigeria).
sources.note: Nothing; these are Glottolog name-matching errors, not Kemak sources.
